transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Thanks. Well, I guess I'm here because of some trouble I've been having with food. What really worries me is that once I start picking at things late at night, I just can't seem to stop. I tell myself that is enough, Santiago, but my hand just keeps going back for more. It is like I don't even get to make the decision anymore.
After eating this way, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, fasting, exercising excessively, or using laxatives?

No, I don't do any of that. I mean, I feel pretty awful about it the next morning, but I don't try to throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. And I'm definitely not exercising like crazy or starving myself. I just... I just kind of live with the guilt and go to work.
How often do these episodes of feeling unable to stop eating happen?

For the past several months, I'd say it's been happening most weeks... at least once a week, anyway. It usually happens on a night when there are plenty of leftovers in the fridge and everyone else in the house has already gone to bed.
During these episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food compared with what most people would eat in similar circumstances?

Yeah, I'd say so. It's a lot of food. Like, on some nights after work, I can go through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, a bunch of tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left in the fridge. And I do all this just standing there in the kitchen, like I'm just cleaning up the leftovers or something. But it's definitely way more than a normal person would eat for a late-night snack.
During these episodes, do you eat much more quickly than you normally would?

Yeah, I do. I eat it pretty fast. It's not like when I'm sitting down having dinner with the family. It's more like... I'm just trying to get it done before anyone wakes up and catches me. I eat so quick I'm barely even tasting the food, to be honest.
How much emotional distress do these episodes cause you?

I guess I'm not really sure how to measure that. I mean, it definitely bothers me. I feel pretty guilty after I do it, especially the next morning when I see the empty containers. But... I don't know if I'd call it severe distress or anything. I just feel bad about it and wish I hadn't done it, and then I just go to work and try to put it out of my mind.
How strongly do these episodes upset or distress you—would you say they cause significant emotional distress or interfere with your daily life?

I wouldn't say it completely stops me from living my life. I mean, I'm still getting to my shipping and receiving shifts on time and handling all my responsibilities at work. But... it does affect things a little bit at home. Lately, I've started avoiding hanging out in the kitchen late at night when the family is still up. I just get worried someone's going to notice how uneasy I am around the food, or that I might start eating and not be able to stop in front of them. So I guess it interferes in that way, just making me pull back from my family a bit.
